#### What type of PR is this?

<!--

/kind regression
-->

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

It is allowed to create a pod with constraints that share the same topologyKey, but the code didn't fully support this. In particular, in some places it assumed that the topologyKey was unique among constraints and was able to overwrite the results of one constraint with the results of another. This PR makes the PodTopologySpread plugin's data structures indexed by the constraint, isolating them.

Additionally, it was easier to make the change by replacing map to slice in PreFilter when iterating through nodes (like in #129025 which will be closed eventually). 

Fix does not affect scheduling throughput of PodTopologySpread plugin. Replacing map to slice increases the scheduling throughput of pods with topology spreading by up to **25%**.

Benchmark | Before [pods/s avg] | After [pods/s avg]
--- | --- | ---
TopologySpreading/5000Nodes | 223 | 269

issue_context.title: PodTopologySpread plugin with multiple constraints with the same topology key incorrectly counts matching pods on node
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

In PodTopologySpread PreFilter, while processing the nodes, their count is not aggregated, but overwritten by the last constraint with the same topologyKey:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/810e9e212ec5372d16b655f57b9231d8654a2179/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/podtopologyspread/filtering.go#L276-L285

Probably, PreScore counting is also wrong, as it probably duplicate the pods:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/810e9e212ec5372d16b655f57b9231d8654a2179/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/podtopologyspread/scoring.go#L164-L180

### What did you expect to happen?

`countPodsMatchSelector` should process all constraints per topologyKey at once to aggregate, but not duplicate the counts for pods on node.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

I found the issue refactoring the plugin's code, but probably unexpected behavior of topology spreading will happen when defining multiple topology spread constraints with the same topologyKey on a single pod.
